title: Order in a map transformation
stem: A horizontal stretch has matrix $S=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and an anticlockwise quarter-turn has matrix $R=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Let $P=(2,3)$. Unless otherwise stated, give numerical answers exactly or to three significant figures.

parts.prompt: Find the combined matrix for S followed by R.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the images of P under S then R, and under R then S.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain whether these transformations commute.

steps.text: Matrices act right to left, so the combined matrix is $RS$.
$RS=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\2&0\end{pmatrix}$.
Evaluate the two ordered matrix products on the point vector.
S then R gives $(-3,4)$.
R then S gives $(-6,2)$.
They do not commute because the two products give different images of P.
The stretch acts along a fixed horizontal direction, which the rotation changes.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the range of positive length scale factors giving a finite total, and state whether there is a largest allowable value.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Give two physical limitations of the infinite design.

Finite manufacturing precision prevents arbitrarily small copies.
The copies may overlap or encounter finite boundary space, invalidating addition of their areas.

stem: The diagram shows three emergency stations A,B,C on a square-kilometre coordinate grid. Each point is assigned to its nearest station by straight-line distance. Unless otherwise stated, give numerical answers exactly or to three significant figures.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the point equidistant from all three stations, and hence state the portion of the AB bisector forming a Voronoi edge.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate its distance from each station and explain its service significance.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Assess the use of Euclidean Voronoi cells for emergency response, giving two refinements.

steps.text: The boundary is the perpendicular bisector of AB.

Equate squared distances to A and C: $9+(y-2)^2=(y-6)^2$.
The A-B Voronoi edge is $x=5$ with $y\leq23/8$; above the vertex C is nearer.
Use the distance to any station.
Distance 3.13 km.
It is a location with the same travel-distance estimate to all three stations.
Straight-line distance ignores roads, barriers and congestion.
Use travel time or a road-network metric where available.
Station capacity or specialist equipment may require weighted service rules.
The nearest station by distance is not always the fastest suitable responder.
